column1: # The superuser decision sites: every non-test function that reads IsSuperuser or names policy.Superuser,
# with its count of reads. The nine places where platform power stood in for organization power (PLAN-10979
# section 1.3; 9 = the auth-service provisioning routes, #5236) no longer read the flag: each decides by an explicit
# platform action and is listed in platform_action_sites.tsv. What is left here is carriage (token claims, wire
# fields, writers, row scans), the Holds methods that turn the flag into the actions platform_admin lists, and the
# platform-only routes that move onto their own actions next (CHAOS-11847 PR-B).
# Reasons for rows that read the flag without deciding a power: Scope.mayImpersonate and Authenticator.accessTokenUser
# read it only to decide whether the request needs the full user read (a claim peek); it may widen a read and grants
# nothing, and Scope.Impersonation decides the session by admin.impersonate. The *.Holds methods are the derivation of the
# actions from the flag. Everything else here is a claim, a wire field, a writer or a row scan.
